## Overview

In continuous time, an individual's trait flows deterministically by a
growth velocity $v(z)$ between random birth and death events. The
population is therefore a *measure-valued piecewise-deterministic Markov
process* (PDMP): deterministic flow punctuated by jumps. Its mean obeys
the physiologically-structured population model (PSPM) transport
equation,

$$
\frac{\partial n}{\partial t} = -\frac{\partial}{\partial z}\big(v(z)\,n\big)
  - \mu(z)\,n + \text{births},
$$

so this is the individual-level dual of the deterministic transport
backend. No dedicated PDMP solver is needed — an operator split (flow
then jumps) over small steps does it.

## Setup

```{julia}
using IndividualBasedPopulationDynamics
using StructuredPopulationCore: ContinuousDomain
using Random, Statistics, Plots
```

The continuous-time IBM is parameterized by per-individual rate
functions of the trait: `flow(x)` (growth velocity), `mortality(x)`,
`fecundity(x)` (birth rate), and `recruit(rng)` (offspring trait).

## Birth–death dynamics

With no flow, constant birth rate $b$ and death rate $d$, the mean
population grows as $N_0 e^{(b-d)t}$:

```{julia}
b, d = 0.6, 0.4
dom = ContinuousDomain(0.0, 10.0, 50)
world = ibm_world_ct(x -> 0.0, x -> d, x -> b, rng -> 2.0, dom;
                     rng = Random.Xoshiro(11), traits0 = fill(2.0, 5000))
res = ibm_run_ct!(world, (0.0, 3.0); dt = 0.01, saveat = 0.25)

plot(res.t, res.N; seriestype = :scatter, label = "IBM",
     xlabel = "time", ylabel = "population size",
     title = "Birth–death: IBM vs N₀ exp((b−d)t)")
plot!(res.t, 5000 .* exp.((b - d) .* res.t); lw = 2, label = "analytic mean")
```

## Advection and mortality

Now let individuals flow at constant velocity $v$ and die at rate $\mu$,
with no births. The population decays by mortality, while the trait
distribution advects rigidly — its mean follows the characteristics,
$\bar z(t) = \bar z(0) + v t$:

```{julia}
v, mu = 1.0, 0.2
dom2 = ContinuousDomain(0.0, 50.0, 100)
world2 = ibm_world_ct(x -> v, x -> mu, x -> 0.0, rng -> 0.0, dom2;
                      rng = Random.Xoshiro(22), traits0 = fill(5.0, 5000))
res2 = ibm_run_ct!(world2, (0.0, 3.0); dt = 0.01, saveat = 0.5, save_traits = true)

mean_traits = [mean(tr) for tr in res2.traits]
plot(res2.t, mean_traits; seriestype = :scatter, label = "IBM mean trait",
     xlabel = "time", ylabel = "mean trait",
     title = "Advection: mean trait follows the characteristics")
plot!(res2.t, 5.0 .+ v .* res2.t; lw = 2, label = "5 + v·t")
```

Mortality-driven decay of the total:

```{julia}
plot(res2.t, res2.N; seriestype = :scatter, label = "IBM",
     xlabel = "time", ylabel = "population size",
     title = "Mortality decay: IBM vs N₀ exp(−μ t)")
plot!(res2.t, 5000 .* exp.(-mu .* res2.t); lw = 2, label = "analytic")
```

## A size-structured example with growth, death and reproduction

Combining all three: individuals grow toward a maximum size, die at a
size-dependent rate, and large individuals reproduce (offspring entering
near a fixed birth size). This is the classic physiologically-structured
IBM:

```{julia}
dom3 = ContinuousDomain(0.0, 5.0, 100)
flow(x)      = 0.6 * (5.0 - x)                 # von Bertalanffy-like growth
mortality(x) = 0.1                             # constant mortality
fecundity(x) = x > 2.0 ? 0.4 : 0.0             # only large individuals reproduce
recruit(rng) = 0.2 + 0.05 * randn(rng)         # offspring near size 0.2

world3 = ibm_world_ct(flow, mortality, fecundity, recruit, dom3;
                      rng = Random.Xoshiro(5), traits0 = fill(0.5, 2000))
res3 = ibm_run_ct!(world3, (0.0, 15.0); dt = 0.01, saveat = 5.0, save_traits = true)

histogram(res3.traits[end]; bins = 0:0.2:5, legend = false,
          xlabel = "size z", ylabel = "count",
          title = "Stationary size distribution (t = 15)")
```

```{julia}
plot(res3.t, res3.N; marker = :circle, legend = false,
     xlabel = "time", ylabel = "population size",
     title = "Approach to a stationary size-structured population")
```

## Summary

- `ibm_world_ct(flow, mortality, fecundity, recruit, domain; ...)` builds
  a continuous-time IBM — the measure-valued PDMP.
- `ibm_step_ct!(world, dt)` / `ibm_run_ct!(world, tspan; dt, saveat)`
  advance it by operator splitting: `Poisson(fecundity·dt)` births,
  death with probability `1 − exp(−mortality·dt)`, then Euler flow.
- The mean reproduces birth–death growth, advective transport (method of
  characteristics), and stationary size structure — i.e. the PSPM
  transport equation — without any dedicated PDMP solver.
